about: Live non-regression of the four root-cause fixes of the 2026-09-19 plan.
Everything this file creates lives under ${SANDBOX} and nowhere else. The campaign's
namespace, user, group and systemd unit are NOT recreated: none of the four fixes touch them.
Teardown is `rm -r --`, never `rm -rf`: `rm\s+-rf` is the first blacklist pattern, so `rm -rf`
is refused with exit 4 and the directory would stay while the run looked clean.
Run it in three phases, not in one shot. run.py dispatches its cases through a thread pool,
so with --jobs 2 the setup, the write cases and the teardown would race:
No sudo case creates ${SANDBOX}: a `mkdir -p` under `sudo` would make the directory root-owned,
and /tmp is sticky, so the unprivileged teardown could then no longer remove it.
H02, H04, H05 and H06 are NOT here and cannot be. H02 asserts on the bridge host's own audit
log, not on a tool's output. H04/H05/H06 need several tool calls inside ONE server process,
because a session lives in the SessionManager of that process and run.py spawns one process per
case (same reason mcp_probe.py exists). They run from H-session.py in this directory.

cases.note: Minimal sandbox. Unprivileged on purpose, so H90 can remove it.
Task 1, the report's own command. Shows the compound still runs under elevation.

Task 1, the DISCRIMINATING case. H01 alone cannot fail: the old prefix form (`sudo -n touch … && echo ok`) elevates the first process and still prints ok. Only a SECOND element that needs root separates them — prefix gives 0\n1000, the shipped wrap `sudo -n bash -c '<all>'` gives 0\n0.
Task 3. 6 = EXIT_REMOTE_FAILURE (src/cli/runner.rs), distinct from the bridge's own 1-5. `exit=` and not `error=`: run.py's `error=` needs rc != 0, which is the very thing D1 used not to deliver.
Task 3 on the MCP path: the result carries isError, which run.py reports as rc != 0. The process exit code 6 is a CLI-only contract, so `exit=6` would be wrong here.

Ruling R20, live. apt-daily.service is loaded and normally inactive (dead), so `systemctl status` exits 3 and Task 3's blanket rule turns a correct, read-only answer into a failure. StandardTool has the opt-out for exactly this (NONZERO_EXIT_IS_ERROR = false, 'a probe whose verdict IS the code') and no tool in the tree sets it. This case asserts the RIGHT answer, so it fails until the opt-out is applied.
Same defect seen from the MCP path: isError on a status query that answered.
Teardown proof: the sandbox is gone.
